clinical_scope.population: Adults and young people aged 16 years or older unless otherwise specified by local protocol
excluded_populations: pediatric specialty pathways unless explicitly validated
clinical_scope.intended_use: High-risk candidate retrieval and guideline-based verification for suspected Ischemic Stroke.
clinical_scope.important_boundary: This graph supports clinical reasoning and missed-diagnosis risk reduction; it is not an autonomous diagnostic system.

distinctions.description: Symptoms overlap; urgent brain imaging is required to distinguish ischemia from hemorrhage before reperfusion decisions.

basic_info.working_definition: Ischemic stroke is acute neurologic dysfunction caused by focal cerebral, spinal, or retinal infarction due to vascular occlusion or hypoperfusion.
why_high_risk_for_missed_diagnosis: Posterior circulation strokes can present with dizziness, vomiting, ataxia, visual symptoms, or headache and be mistaken for benign vertigo.
Symptoms may fluctuate or improve, leading to under-triage despite TIA/stroke risk.
Hypoglycemia, seizure, migraine, intoxication, and intracranial hemorrhage can mimic stroke.
Delayed last-known-well assessment or imaging can miss reperfusion windows.
basic_info.time_sensitivity: Requires immediate stroke-code workflow, last-known-well determination, urgent brain/vascular imaging, and reperfusion eligibility assessment.

activation_logic.minimum_activation: Sudden focal neurologic deficit, BE-FAST symptom, acute disabling neurologic syndrome, or unexplained acute posterior circulation symptoms.

case_features: facial droop or arm weakness or speech difficulty

strong_activation_patterns.reason: TIA/stroke warning event requiring urgent evaluation.

weak_activation_patterns.reason: Nonspecific but posterior circulation stroke may still need context.

symptom_to_candidate_retrieval.scoring_warning: Weights are for retrieval and explanation only. They are not calibrated probabilities and must not be used as a diagnostic score.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Are symptoms sudden and focal or consistent with BE-FAST/posterior circulation stroke?
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: Lower priority but assess mimics and atypical stroke.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: What is last-known-well and symptom discovery time?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Use time window for reperfusion eligibility.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: If outside window, still evaluate for thrombectomy/secondary prevention as applicable.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Is glucose checked and are common stroke mimics considered?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Treat mimic if found while continuing stroke pathway if uncertainty remains.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: Proceed if no mimic explains deficit.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Is urgent brain imaging available to distinguish ischemia from hemorrhage?
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: If hemorrhage present, switch to ICH pathway.
guideline_verification_pathway.if_missing: Cannot classify stroke type without imaging.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Is large vessel occlusion assessed when clinically indicated?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Evaluate thrombectomy eligibility and transfer needs.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: What is deficit severity and disability level?
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: Minor nondisabling symptoms may follow local pathway.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Does the case meet local criteria for thrombolysis or thrombectomy evaluation?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Recommend stroke-team pathway; do not generate autonomous orders.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: Document why not eligible if data allow.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Could ICH, seizure, migraine, hypoglycemia, vestibular disorder, or dissection explain the presentation?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Report competing conditions and parallel verification.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: AIS remains most supported if imaging/clinical pattern aligns.

distinguishing_features: Same focal deficits; severe headache, vomiting, reduced consciousness, anticoagulation, or very high BP may raise concern.
Witnessed seizure, tongue bite, postictal confusion, deficit resolving over time.
Can mimic focal deficits or altered mental status.
Gradual spread of positive neurologic symptoms, migraine history; still avoid premature closure in first/worst or atypical cases.
Isolated continuous vertigo without focal neurologic signs; posterior stroke remains concern if ataxia, direction-changing nystagmus, or vascular risk.
Stroke symptoms plus chest/back pain, pulse deficit, hypotension, or aortic risk factors.

final_assessment.safety_statement: Clinical decision support only; urgent clinician assessment is required when a high-risk condition is suspected.

evidence_sources.title: 2026 AHA/ASA Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke
evidence_sources.publisher: American Heart Association / American Stroke Association
key_points: Provides updated evidence-based recommendations for acute ischemic stroke management from prehospital evaluation through acute reperfusion strategies.
Supports stroke-code activation, last-known-well assessment, urgent brain and vascular imaging, thrombolysis and thrombectomy eligibility evaluation, and management of mimics.

evidence_sources.title: Signs and Symptoms of Stroke
evidence_sources.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
key_points: Stroke warning symptoms include sudden weakness/numbness, confusion or speech trouble, visual difficulty, trouble walking/dizziness/loss of balance, and sudden severe headache.
Used for symptom normalization and emergency-recognition nodes.

must_not: Do not make an autonomous definitive diagnosis.
Do not use a single symptom, sign, laboratory result, score, or imaging clue as a standalone rule-in or rule-out criterion.
Do not provide patient-facing reassurance when critical red-flag data are missing.
Do not ignore competing high-risk differential diagnoses.
Do not replace local emergency, specialty, or hospital protocols.
Do not generate medication orders; recommend clinician-led pathway activation instead.
Do not exclude stroke because symptoms improved.
Do not label isolated dizziness benign without posterior circulation red-flag assessment.
Do not decide thrombolysis without imaging and stroke-team/local protocol.
must_do: Use this graph for candidate retrieval, missed-diagnosis risk reduction, and guideline-based verification.
Separate supporting evidence, evidence against, and missing critical information.
State whether verification is complete, partial, impossible from available data, or contradicted.
Include differential diagnoses that can mimic the condition.
Trace guideline-dependent claims to evidence IDs.
Mark output as clinical decision support requiring qualified clinician review.
Always state whether brain imaging has ruled out hemorrhage.
Always evaluate LVO status when severe/cortical signs are present.
